purpose: Test whether the apparent 5' UTR / ORF coupling survives bounding the base-pair span.
method: Identical 5' UTR and 3' UTR, two ORF contexts (Fluc 1653 nt, Fluc-PEST 1776 nt, differing only by a 123 nt insert at position 1650). Folded at several ViennaRNA max_bp_span values; all other settings identical to the standard worker (Turner 2004, 37 C, dangles 2).
metric: mean unpaired probability over the 44 nt 5' UTR
finding: The coupling vanishes once base pairs are bounded. At a span of 200 nt or less the 5' UTR folds identically in both ORF contexts to four decimal places. The entire effect requires base pairs spanning more than 600 nt.
interpretation: The apparent UTR-ORF coupling is a property of unbounded global folding, not a robust sequence property. The sequence difference between the two contexts lies 1650 nt downstream of the 5' UTR, so only a very long-range pair can transmit it.
corrects: reports/construct_comparison_fluc_vs_fluc_pest_2026-10-19.md, which reported the coupling without establishing its mechanism and drew a design conclusion from it.
no_claim: No statement is made about which span is physically correct.
Every uridine is N1-methylpseudouridine, which ViennaRNA does not represent.
This is a model-behaviour result, not a measurement of RNA structure.
